title: Grill — broken preview for images picked with the Files Picker
summary:
**12 decisions** before this gets planned, plus a confirm list of 6 defaults. Start with **Q1, how a user-picked image in a protected folder gets a thumbnail**. It is the only security-posture call, and most of the other questions depend on it.

The short version of the investigation (`docs/plans/picked-image-preview-tcc-investigation.md`): since #281, `/files/preview` reads image bytes through a *disclaimed* child (`sh` → `stat` → `cat`). macOS TCC denies that child access to `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents` and `~/Downloads` without a prompt, so the core answers **403**. The chip then treats any failure as "not found": it turns amber and blocks the click, even though `/open-path` would open the file.

Your progress is saved in the browser as you go.

proven.text: **Root cause, proven by a spike.** The disclaimed reader's `stat` succeeds on `~/Desktop/Screenshot … PM.png`, and `cat` then fails immediately with `Operation not permitted` and no prompt. The core maps that to `denied`, then 403. A copy of the same bytes in the scratchpad reads fine.

evidence.label: 403 on denied

proven.text: **The chip turns any failure into "not found" and blocks the click.** `onStatus` calls `onMissing()` on any non-`ok` status. A click on a missing chip opens the not-found dialog without calling `/open-path`.

proven: **Agents in tmux can read the original picked file.** This grill step runs as Claude Code in Agetor's tmux, and it read `~/Desktop/Screenshot 2026-11-18 at 2.40.41 PM.png` with its Read tool. Your screenshot shows the amber chip. Copying a picked image is therefore **not** needed for claude-code to see it. It only matters for the thumbnail, and possibly for the ACP harnesses (Q11).

**A Finder drag already copies.** A dragged png/jpg/gif/webp is uploaded to `~/.agetor/screenshots/screenshot-<utc-ts>-<id>.png`, so the original filename is lost. That folder holds **573 files, 117 MB** on your machine, and **nothing ever cleans it** (no retention or delete path touches it).

**Opening non-image attachments works.** They call `/open-path`, which runs `existsSync` in-process and then LaunchServices. Only thumbnailed images break: attachment chips, markdown images, `SendUserFile` tiles, and binary-diff previews in protected folders.

**The native open panel runs in the core process.** `/refs/pick` → `openFileDialogLabelled` → `native.openFileDialog`, Electrobun over FFI in Bun. A copy made at pick time is made by the process that holds your intent grant (`com.apple.macl` is on the picked files). Confirm item C1 adds a spike that proves this doesn't prompt.

**The security constraint behind D26(j) still applies.** User bubbles are rebuilt from the agent-writable claude JSONL, and `agetor.sqlite` is agent-writable. So "this path is in a user bubble" is not proof that you picked it. An in-process read keyed on either one reopens the hole #281 closed.

sections.title: How a picked image gets a thumbnail
sections.intro: Every option keeps the **honest chip** (Q5–Q7) as the floor: whenever no thumbnail can be shown, the chip says so and still opens the file. The question is what we add on top of it.

questions.title: Which mechanism gives user-picked images in protected folders a thumbnail?
questions.why: Decides whether the agent's prompt path changes, whether new storage appears, and whether the D26(j) boundary moves.
questions.context: The investigation recommended **(A) copy and reference the copy**. Since then I proved that agents in tmux read the original fine. That makes A's main cost (the agent gets `~/.agetor/…` instead of your file, so an *"optimise this image"* edits a copy) look avoidable. I now recommend a variant of B that needs **no stored mapping**: at pick time, while the core holds your intent grant, copy the bytes to `dataDir/previews/<sha256(path)>.<ext>`. `/files/preview` first tries the original (disclaimed). If that is **denied**, it reads the twin, also disclaimed. An agent that plants a fake twin can only make a thumbnail show bytes it already controls in a non-protected folder. That is the same risk a worktree markdown image carries today, so D26(j) holds.

options.label: Preview twin keyed by path, original path kept in the prompt (B′)
options.description: Copy at pick time to `dataDir/previews/<sha256(path)>.<ext>`. Thumbnails fall back to the twin only when the original read is denied.
options.consequence: The agent and the chip still show your real file name and location. Adds one cache folder that can be evicted (Q4). Old messages get no thumbnail (honest chip).

options.label: Copy and reference the copy (A)
options.description: Same as Finder drag: the prompt carries `~/.agetor/screenshots/…` (or attachments).
options.consequence: Consistent with drag, and every harness can read the copy. The agent never sees or edits your original. The copies are agent inputs, so they can't be evicted.

options.label: In-memory provenance set (C)
options.description: Paths returned by `/refs/pick` this launch are read in-process.
options.consequence: No storage. Every thumbnail disappears after a restart, which is most of the time for long tasks.

options.label: Click-to-load (D)
options.description: "Preview blocked by macOS · click to load". Your click triggers one in-process read.
options.consequence: No storage. An agent can lure you into clicking a path it chose. This moves the D26(j) line.

options.label: No thumbnail: honest chip only (F)
options.description: Just fix the chip: "preview unavailable", and the click opens the file.
options.consequence: Smallest change. Picked Desktop images never show a thumbnail.

options.label: Relax D26(j) for reference-block paths (E)
options.description: Read paths listed under `Referenced files/folders:` in-process.
options.consequence: **Reopens the confused-deputy hole**, because bubbles and the DB are agent-writable. Not recommended.

recommendation.reason: You get a thumbnail without changing what the agent receives or relaxing D26(j), and the twin is a cache that can be evicted, so it never piles up the way screenshots/ does.

questions.title: Which entry points create the twin or copy?
questions.why: Each entry point is a server route to touch and test.
questions.context: A **Finder drag** of png/jpg/gif/webp already uploads to `screenshots/` (rung 3), so it needs nothing. The others keep original paths today. `/refs/resolve` is `app+cli`, so only the **app** caller may trigger a copy, since a CLI caller is not you clicking.

evidence.label: drag pasteboard excludes the 4 uploadable types

options.label: Files Picker (`/refs/pick`, files mode)
options.consequence: The reported bug.

options.label: Paste of a Finder-copied file (`file://` → `/refs/resolve`, app caller only)
options.consequence: Same symptom today, same fix.

options.label: Finder drag of a non-uploadable image (heic, svg, bmp, ico, avif via `/refs/drag`)
options.consequence: These keep their original path today and break the same way.

recommendation.reason: All three are "the user pointed at this file" gestures through app-only paths, and skipping one leaves the same broken chip reachable.

questions.title: Which image types get a twin or copy?

options.label: All 10 `isImagePath` types (png jpg jpeg gif webp svg bmp ico avif heic)
options.consequence: Every chip that tries a thumbnail can get one.

options.label: Only the 4 `SCREENSHOT_UPLOADABLE` types
options.consequence: heic/svg/avif picks still show the honest chip.

recommendation.reason: The chip decides whether to thumbnail with `isImagePath`, so the copy rule should match it, or a picked .heic stays broken.

questions.title: What is the largest file that gets a twin or copy?
questions.context: Drag uploads (`/screenshots`) cap at **25 MB**, and `/files/preview` serves up to **50 MB**. Above the cap there is no copy, and the chip shows the honest "preview unavailable" state.

recommendation.reason: Matches the drag-upload cap, so drag and pick behave the same for the same file.

questions.title: How long do preview twins live?
questions.why: Twins are only a cache. Losing one turns that chip into the honest "preview unavailable" chip, nothing worse.

options.label: Size-capped cache: evict the oldest past a total cap, swept at boot and after each write
options.consequence: Bounded disk use. Very old messages lose their thumbnails.

options.label: Delete with the task (when no other task's refs list the path)
options.consequence: Tied to task lifetime. Follow-up refs exist only in events, so the check is approximate.

options.label: Keep forever, like screenshots/
options.consequence: Simplest. Grows without bound (screenshots/ is at 117 MB already).

recommendation.reason: A cache whose loss is harmless should be bounded by size, not by a lifecycle we would have to approximate.

questions.title: What is the total size cap for the preview-twin cache?

recommendation.reason: Holds about 100 Retina screenshots, roughly 4× today's screenshots/ total, and still small on any Mac.

questions.title: How long do copies referenced in the prompt live?
questions.why: The agent may re-read a copy on any later turn, so it can't be evicted the way a cache can.

options.label: Keep forever, like screenshots/ today
options.consequence: Consistent with drag. Unbounded growth stays an open problem.

options.label: Delete when the task is deleted
options.consequence: Needs a record of which task owns which copy (a new server-managed column or a folder per task).

recommendation.reason: Ties the copy to the only thing that reads it, and avoids adding to the 117 MB that nothing cleans.

sections.title: The honest chip (the floor in every option)
sections.intro: Rule from `AttachmentChips.tsx:73-87` and the original spec (`improve-image-attached-message-ui.md:17`): only a **404** proves a file is gone. Everything else means "we can't show a preview", not "not found". `SentFilesCard` already follows this rule.

questions.title: Should a 403 get its own blob status, with wording about macOS privacy?

options.label: New `denied` status (403), separate from `error`
options.description: `statusForHttp(403)` → `denied`. The chip says macOS privacy blocks the preview. Other errors say "preview unavailable".
options.consequence: One more union member to wire through `AuthedImg`, `MdImage` and `BinaryFilePreview`. Honest, specific copy.

options.label: Reuse `error` with one generic "Preview unavailable"
options.consequence: Smaller diff. The user doesn't learn why.

recommendation.reason: A 403 here always means a macOS-protected folder, and saying so tells you the file is fine and why the preview is missing.

questions.title: How does the "preview unavailable" chip look?

options.label: Neutral (muted border, `ImageOff`), amber kept for 404 only
options.preview:
[⊘ Screenshot 2026-11-18 at 2.40.41 PM.png]   ← muted, clickable, opens in Preview
 tooltip: "Preview blocked by macOS privacy (Desktop). Click to open."

[⚠ old-shot.png]   ← amber: file is gone (404) → not-found dialog
options.consequence: Amber means "gone" again.

options.label: Keep amber for every failure, change only the tooltip and the click
options.consequence: Still reads as "broken" at a glance.

recommendation.reason: Amber is a warning, and the file is fine, so a warning color repeats the misleading signal that started this report.

questions.title: What do the chip tooltips say? Edit as needed.

recommendation.value:
denied (403): "Preview blocked by macOS privacy — Agetor can't read files in this folder for previews. Click to open."
error / timeout: "Preview unavailable. Click to open."
too-large (413): "Too large to preview. Click to open."
missing (404): "Image not found: <path>" (unchanged)
recommendation.reason: Each one says what happened and that the click still works.

questions.title: Which surfaces get the 404-vs-other split and the new wording?
questions.context: `MdImage` keeps its walk over candidate paths (any non-ok moves to the next one), and only its final fallback title changes. Its click already opens. `BinaryFilePreview` is the diff's binary pane. It would only hit 403 for an `isolation: "none"` task whose workdir is in a protected folder.

options.label: `AttachmentChips` (the reported bug; the click must reach `/open-path`)
`MdImage` fallback chip (today titled "Image not found" for a 403)
`SentFilesCard` (behavior already right; wording only, for consistency)
`BinaryFilePreview` pane copy for 403

recommendation.reason: One `denied` status should read the same everywhere it renders; leaving one surface saying "not found" is the same bug in another place.

sections.title: Agent-chosen images, old messages, adjacent risk

questions.title: How should agent-chosen images in protected folders behave (markdown `![](~/Documents/x.png)`, SendUserFile of a Desktop file)?
questions.why: This is exactly the D26(j) threat: an agent picks a path and the webview fetches it.

options.label: Honest "blocked" chip that still opens; no thumbnail
options.consequence: D26(j) unchanged. Your click goes to LaunchServices (the app you chose), never to a core read.

options.label: Offer click-to-load there too
options.consequence: An agent can lure a click that makes Agetor read a protected file in-process.

recommendation.reason: Agent-chosen paths are the case #281 closed on purpose. Opening the file stays one click away, so there's little to gain from relaxing it.

questions.title: For messages already sent with protected-folder refs (this pipeline's own prompts included), is "preview unavailable, click opens" enough?
questions.context: Persisted events stay raw, and the core can't read the originals without your gesture, so the only way back to thumbnails is C or D. With B′, re-attaching the same file later would create its twin, and the old chips would then light up too, because the twin is keyed by path.

options.label: Yes: honest chip, click opens
options.consequence: No extra work.

options.label: No: they must get thumbnails back
options.consequence: Requires C or D on top of the chosen mechanism.

recommendation.reason: The file opens with one click, and adding a second read path to bring back old thumbnails isn't worth what it costs in security.

questions.title: Cursor and fx run disclaimed **without** tmux, so they may be unable to read a picked Desktop file at all. In this change?
questions.context: This is unproven. It follows from the spike, where the disclaimed `cat` was denied, and from the fact that `cursor-acp.ts` and `fx-acp.ts` spawn without tmux. Agents in tmux (claude) read it fine, as shown above. It is a different symptom (the agent can't read the file, rather than a missing thumbnail), but it has the same cause. (A) copy-on-pick would fix it as a side effect. B′ would not.

options.label: In this change: spike it, and if it's broken, fix it here
options.consequence: Bigger scope. The fix shape is unknown until the spike runs.

options.label: Spike in this change; if broken, open a separate ticket with the evidence
options.consequence: Proves the risk now, keeps this fix focused.

options.label: Out of scope entirely: separate ticket now
options.consequence: Nothing proven in this change.

recommendation.reason: It is a different user-visible bug in other harnesses. Proving it costs one spike, while fixing it may need its own design (copy for ACP only, or a tmux host).

questions.title: Should `BinaryFilePreview` of an `isolation: "none"` task in a protected folder get more than the wording fix?
questions.context: Those bytes are written by the agent (the diff's new side), so they are agent-chosen, and only the honest-chip treatment is safe there.

options.label: Wording only (via Q8), no thumbnail mechanism
options.consequence: Consistent with Q9.

options.label: Leave it entirely as is
options.consequence: Keeps today's generic error copy there.

recommendation.reason: Same `denied` status, same copy, no new read path.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: These are defaults I'd bet on. One click each.

questions.title: Pick-time spike before building

recommendation.value: Before the twin or copy work is built, the plan runs a dev-build spike (`~/.agetor-dev`): pick a `~/Desktop` image through the real NSOpenPanel and verify that the core's in-process copy succeeds **without** an "Agetor would like to access Desktop" prompt. If it prompts, stop and come back to you with the honest chip only.
recommendation.reason: Investigation assumption 1 (the intent grant covers the core) is consistent with the evidence but not proven.

questions.title: Twin lookup order

recommendation.value: `/files/preview` first tries the original (disclaimed, as today). Only on `denied` does it look up `previews/<sha256(path)>`, read through the same disclaimed `openFileBytes`. A readable original always wins, so the thumbnail stays current.
recommendation.reason: Never shows a stale twin when the real file is readable, and keeps one reader.

questions.title: Tests

recommendation.value: A new Playwright spec, `e2e/attachment-chips.spec.ts`, with `AGETOR_FAKE_PICK_REFS_DIR` and a `chmod 000` png. It asserts: (1) the chip shows the preview-unavailable state, not amber; (2) a click reaches `/open-path`, not the not-found dialog; (3) a deleted file still shows amber and the not-found dialog; (4) with the twin, a picked file that is then `chmod 000` still thumbnails. Plus unit tests: `statusForHttp(403)`, the twin write/lookup/eviction, and the `/refs/resolve` CLI caller never creating a twin.
recommendation.reason: Nothing pins the chip's behavior on a 403 today (investigation §2), so a naive fix could pass green without proving the UI.

questions.title: Docs

recommendation.value: Update `docs/architecture/security.md` (D26(j) scope: name attachment chips, and state the twin rule), `docs/architecture/markdown-images.md` (403 copy), and `docs/architecture/testing-seams.md` (chmod-000 idiom for chips). Add a dated note to `docs/plans/improve-image-attached-message-ui.md`.
recommendation.reason: CLAUDE.md requires a subsystem doc to change with its behavior.

questions.title: Source of truth

recommendation.value: The plan restates the symptom in-repo (the amber chip, the click that won't open). Your Desktop screenshot is **not** committed.
recommendation.reason: The screenshot only shows Agetor UI, but it lives outside the repo, and a text restatement is enough for review.

questions.title: No CLI/TUI parity work

recommendation.value: `agetor send` builds the same references block but never renders thumbnails, so there is nothing to mirror there.
recommendation.reason: Investigation §5 propagation surface.
